newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T. prepared to look at litigation proposals.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T. prepared to look at litigation proposals.

text.p: B.A.T Industries Plc chairman Lord Cairns said on Friday the group would be prepared to evaluate proposals which would provide relief from current and future U.S. tobacoo litigation.
Referring to speculation the company might demerge its tobacco and financial services interests, Cairns told shareholders at the annual meeting that "our minds are open and there are no sacred cows".

He said, "The good performance we anticipate from our operations around the world will be held back at the pre-tax level if the strength of sterling persists, as the majority of our profits are earned in overseas currencies."
Cairns told shareholders that the U.S tobacco industry remains confident of its ability to win cases and has no intention of proposing a settlement.
He said the company, which sells U.S. blends as part of its global cigarette brand portfolio, thinks it will take an act of Congress to ensure a settlement in the interests of shareholders.

The U.S. industry is currently facing a raft of lawsuits by litigants claiming ill health from smoking, and the companies are holding discussions with plaintiffs over an industry-wide settlement of these legal disputes.

Cairns reiterated the company's stance on demerging its finacial services business from its tobacco operation, saying if any change in its corporate structure would create better value for shareholders, then the company "would not hesitate to propose it".
